title.en: Palayakkarars and the first resistance in Tamil Nadu

text.en: After the Carnatic Wars the East India Company began to extend its power in the south. The local chieftains, called Palayakkarars, did not accept it quietly. Their wars are the first chapter of resistance to British rule in Tamil Nadu.

A palayam means a domain or little kingdom; the system was introduced in Tamil Nadu by Viswanatha Nayaka of Madurai in 1529 with his minister Ariyanathar.
Traditionally there were 72 Palayakkarars who collected revenue, administered territory, settled disputes and kept law and order through Padikaval or Arasu Kaval.
The system lasted about two hundred years until the British took over; eastern palayams included Sattur, Ettayapuram and Panchalankurichi, western ones Uthumalai and Singampatti.
The first resistance came from Puli Thevar of Nerkattumseval, who tried to get help from Hyder Ali and the French.
Other leaders followed: Velunachiyar, Veerapandiya Kattabomman, the Marudhu brothers and Dheeran Chinnamalai.
These Palayakkarars Wars were crushed by the Company's better arms and organisation, but they kept the spirit of resistance alive.
The struggle culminated in the Vellore Revolt of 1806.

problem.en: Why could the British defeat the Palayakkarars even though they fought bravely?

text.en: The chieftains were divided and sometimes fought each other.
The Company had modern firearms, cannons and a trained army.
Help from Hyder Ali or the French did not arrive in time.

prompt.en: Who were the Palayakkarars and why are they remembered?
